Why: JOIN combines related tables. INNER JOIN keeps matching rows; LEFT JOIN keeps all left-side rows and fills unmatched right-side values with NULL. RIGHT JOIN keeps all right-side rows, while FULL OUTER JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both sides; support varies by DBMS. CROSS JOIN produces every possible pair. A self join relates rows within the same table. ON states the relationship explicitly; a one-to-many relationship can produce several result rows for one left-side row.
